title: Sustained Improvement in Facial Skin Quality After Fractional CO2 Laser-Assisted Delivery of Hyaluronic Acid, Ascorbic Acid, and Sodium DNA
content: Laser‐assisted drug delivery may enhance the cutaneous effects of topical agents applied after ablative fractional resurfacing, but clinical data on the combined delivery of hyaluronic acid, ascorbic acid, and sodium DNA are scarce. In this prospective, single‐center, single‐arm pilot study (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07376148), 30 adults with moderate facial photoaging (Fitzpatrick skin types I–III) received one session of fractional CO2 laser followed immediately by topical application of the three agents. Skin quality was graded with the Scientific Assessment Scale of Skin Quality (SASSQ; 0–24 points) and satisfaction with three FACE‐Q Aesthetics domains at baseline, 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months. All participants completed follow‐up. The total SASSQ score decreased from 18.63 ± 2.55 at baseline to 3.73 ± 1.93 at 3 months (80.0% reduction; p < 0.001), and every participant improved by at least 1 point in all six parameters. The median total FACE‐Q score increased from 4.5 to 12.0 (p < 0.001), and no parameter worsened in any participant. This approach was associated with sustained improvement in facial skin quality and high satisfaction; however, the uncontrolled design with unblinded assessment precludes isolating the contribution of the topical agents, and randomized split‐face trials with blinded evaluation are needed.
